newsitem.title: JAPAN: Most TOCOM precious metals slip, palladium firmer.
newsitem.headline: Most TOCOM precious metals slip, palladium firmer.

text.p: Most yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures ended weaker on Friday as buying interest ebbed late in the day pressured by the yen's firmer tone against the dollar, traders said.
Only palladium futures settled mostly firmer, although early gains were pared on the yen's gains.
Most-active benchmark February gold was off 10 yen per gram at 1,361 yen. Other gold prices ranged from 11 yen per gram lower to one yen firmer.
Spot gold was quoted at $352.25/75 per ounce at 0729 GMT, against $351.90/352.40 in New York on Thursday.
In gold futures, active buying emerged from the outset, but buying interest lost steam in line with a slip in bullion prices and the stronger yen.
Traders said further losses in gold futures were likely to be limited as private investors might hunt for bargains unless the yen turned sharply higher against the dollar.

Platinum futures retraced from early gains to end mostly weaker. "A widening spread between gold and platinum, prompted private investors buying gold while selling platinum for most of the day," a senior trader at a foreign bank said.
